# Remedy

> Remedy replaces mail-in coupons and inbox photo checks with a live refund program for any CPSC recall. Owners prove the product destroyed on a live camera with a one-time code. Five checks stop stolen and generated photos, and PayPal Payouts sends the refund within a minute. Recall teams run it all from one console, with analytics and a CPSC report drafted for them.

This is the long version of https://remedy-recalls.vercel.app/llms.txt.

## Checks
Every claim runs the same five checks, in this order. The first three run before any AI.
1. Live camera session. Photos must arrive inside this claim's 10-minute camera session. An image made anywhere else is refused before the model sees it.
2. Never seen before. Every photo is fingerprinted and compared with every earlier claim. A reposted or lightly edited photo is refused.
3. One claim per verified PayPal account. PayPal must report the account as verified, and it gets one claim per recall. A claim farm would need a verified PayPal account for every claim.
4. The code, character by character. The model reads the hand-written code and the product label. K7Q written on a claim issued K7P is a reject.
5. Destroyed as the notice says. The model confirms each step the notice asks for, such as "cut fully in half", and that the photo isn't of a screen or a print.

## Decision rule
- AI reads the photo. It never moves the money.
- Any "no" rejects the claim.
- Any "unclear" holds the claim for a person at the company.
- Only a claim where every check passes is paid.

## Results (fraud benchmark, 7 Nov 2026)
Remedy's photo check faced real owner photos, official recall photos, photos of screens and monitors, other pillows, AI fakes from news coverage, wrong codes, misspelt labels and models that aren't recalled.
- Genuine claims: every one paid.
- Stolen web photos: none paid. No public photo carries a claim's one-time code.
- Wrong codes: every one rejected. The code is read character by character, so K7Q on a claim issued K7P is refused.
- Wrong labels and unrecalled models: every one rejected, including a misspelt X-VESOLIE label.
- Cost: about 1.1¢ to check a claim.
- Speed: claim RM-0442 was paid 15 seconds after its photo.
- Photos that show a claim code were generated for the benchmark, since no public photo carries one. The rest are real web photos and official recall photos.

## Why the camera is the defence
- Remedy never trusts a model alone with the money. Photos enter only through the claim's live camera, inside a 10-minute session, with a one-time code, from a verified PayPal account, and a fixed rule moves the money.

## Console features
- Claims queue on AG Grid: every claim with its photos, each check's result, the model's quoted answers and the payout.
- Evidence panel: the photos at full size, the code the tag must read, and what decided a held or refused claim.
- Review: approve or reject a held claim. Approving runs the duplicate and account checks again, then pays through PayPal Payouts in one step.
- Insights on AG Studio: recall progress against units sold, where claims stop, why claims were refused, time from photo to PayPal, and a recall analyst that answers from the claim records.
- CPSC progress report: a draft built from the claim records, ready to print or save as a PDF.
- Import a recall from its CPSC notice: Remedy drafts the checks from the notice, and the company publishes one claim link.

## Payouts
- Refunds go to each owner's verified PayPal account through PayPal Payouts.
- Terms, including how payouts run on this site: https://remedy-recalls.vercel.app/terms
